sentences.text: Heard learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner and learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing on behalf of the State.

66(D) of IT Act.
And Section 8/12/14 of the POCSO Act.
3. The allegation against the petitioner, who is the tutor of the victim, kidnapped the complainant aged about 17 years, as to force her for illicit intercourse/marriage with another person.

sentences.text: , complainant went alongwith petitioner to Delhi and returned therefrom after passing of substantial period of time, upon instigation of her parents, the present complaint was lodged after about eight months of the alleged occurrence.
It is submitted that the statement of victim recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. appears tutoured and, moreover, the matter now stands compromised between the parties.

5. Learned APP duly assisted by learned counsel Mr. Abhijeet Kumar Singh, appearing on behalf of the informant could not disputed the submission as advanced by learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and further affirmed that matter compromised between the parties 6.

Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances and by taking note of fact as the first case lodged by the father of the informant regarding kidnapping and sexual assault of complainant found false whereafter the present complaint case was lodged after 6-7 months of the alleged occurrence,
where Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.89842 of 2024(3) dt.08-05-2025 prima facie, it appears that the victim accompanied petitioner up to Delhi and lived together for substantial period of time,
where matter also said to be compromised between the parties, accordingly, above named petitioner, in the event of his arrest or surrender before the learned trial Court, within a period of four weeks of the order, is directed to be released on bail furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/-
(Rupees Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Addl. Sessions Judge VI-cum-Special Court (POCS)), Samastipur/concerned Court, where the case is pending in connection with Samastipur Mahila P.S. Case No. 54 of 2022, subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Cr.P.C./482(2) of the BNSS.
